EQUIVALENT (9). U1 and T1, the out parameters' initial value set to 0: it is left only on a false return, TryReadXRefStream stores the digits only past a true one, and the other callers discard them. U2 and U3, TryParseUnrecordedAt gives 0 or the offset: only KeepsItsPlace's check parses through it, and its record is local, never the stream an /XRefStm read or names again, which are the only records whose DigitsAt the search reads. D3, '?? -1' becomes '?? -2': with no stream read, both lie before every place. N8, '<' becomes '<=' in the inside-the-number arm: a candidate equal to the stream's start maps to that start, a no-op. Its first run was 'killed' by ObjectRuleTests.A_run_of_links_the_walk_takes_at_the_reader_s_deepest_load_is_never_where_the_stack_cuts_it under five parallel workers; it survived the suite when run alone, so that kill was load-induced. N9, '>' becomes '>=': the byte at a header's number's end is white space, or a comment's %, while a reading starts at a token past the white space and comments the offset falls short by, so NumberEnd never equals the stream's start. X1, the initializer -1 removed: DigitsAt is read only of a stream's record, which TryReadXRefStream gives digits where it sets the kind to Stream (the one place), and RelocateTo copies both. X2, RelocateTo copies 0: a stream found moved starts at the header the search found, either at its digit, read with no sign so that its digits start where its reading did, or at the first sign of a header a comment parts, at whose digits the walk finds no header.

SURVIVING, to be filed as debt (2): G2b, IsTokenOnItsLine's new before-the-span guard never taken, and G5, the guard shifted to 'at < -1'. They differ only where the line test is asked of a place before the window. Only the stream an /XRefStm read, told by its digits, can be such a place, and only where that stream, read whole by the /XRefStm, reads again unreadable, typed and not cut by a value when the /Prev's search tries it. No input I could build does that: a cut value short-circuits before the line test, and guards and caches repeat the first reading. The guard stays as a defensive branch (invariant 4): it keeps a slice before the span from throwing.
deviations: NumberRunsInto's sign arm, the look at an all-sign run in the window, is removed together with the 'streamStart >= spanStart' guard, rather than keeping the guard 'for the arm it still serves'. Reason: the new digits test subsumes the sign arm. A header the walk finds past an all-sign run from a + where the reading started lies at that reading's digits. The inside-the-number arm needs no guard: a candidate before the stream's start lies in the window, so that start does too, and with streamStart -1 the arm is false. The body is now 'candidate == streamDigits || (candidate < streamStart && NumberEnd(...) > streamStart)'.

The position comes from what the load already lexed. A new internal PdfObjectParser.HeaderDigits is set in TryReadIndirectObject from the number token. It is carried out of TryParseNumberedAt, TryParseUnrecordedAt and TryParseNearHybridPrev by a new out parameter, and kept as XRefSectionRecord.DigitsAt (default -1, copied by RelocateTo) on every stream record. It is read only of the stream the /XRefStm read or names again. Nothing is read for it.

I added a guard not named in the task, `if (at < 0) return false;` at the top of IsTokenOnItsLine. The mapping can now give a place before the window, the mapped stream's start. The look for a section the chain reached already handles it: HeaderTokenStart returns it unchanged and StartsWithin looks at that one position. The line test would slice before the span, but only on a path no input reaches, where the stream re-reads unreadable. It is a private, defensive branch and stays uncovered.
